findings.title: Clearing a controlled field after submit raises a required error
findings.suggested_fix: Distinguish user-originated from programmatic changes (a ref set in onChange, i.e. the `processedValueRef` the PR body describes) and, for programmatic changes, use the revalidate-only path `validation.commit(serializedValue, true)` instead of `validation.change(serializedValue)`: it clears a resolved error and returns early when the field is not currently invalid (useFieldValidation.ts:169-172), so a reset cannot raise a new error. Assumption: a value set from code should resolve stale errors but not surface new ones. This needs the `commit` type in UseFieldValidationReturnValue widened to accept `revalidate`, and the new test 'syncs state and validates when the controlled value changes programmatically' re-scoped, so the maintainer should confirm the intended semantics (sibling controls share the same behavior).

findings.title: Controlled change handler bails out; described two-path guard absent

`details.cancel()` semantics are partial: in uncontrolled mode the DOM text, `data-dirty` and `data-filled` still update while validation and error clearing are skipped (scratch run: validate 0 calls, dirty and filled set, input value 'a', 'Server error' still shown), so a field can keep a stale error for new text; in controlled mode `cancel()` has no effect when the consumer still commits the value (validate still called once). A controlled value changed from code while the control is disabled now invokes the consumer's `validate` and marks the field dirty (scratch run: base 0 calls / not dirty, head 1 call / dirty); visible validity stays suppressed while disabled.

Consumer coverage: only in-repo consumers were checked (the `Input` wrapper, the react-hook-form and TanStack Form handbook demos, existing Field/Form tests). External consumers of the published package are not visible.
testing_gaps: The new test 'renders once per keystroke for controlled input changes' only covers the default validation mode before any submit. 'does not validate when the change is canceled' covers only an uncontrolled control and only asserts that `validate` is not called; nothing pins dirty/filled/Form-error state after `details.cancel()` or the controlled-mode behavior where `cancel()` is ignored if the consumer still sets the value.
